subject: URGENT: Unusual sign-in detected – account suspended
body: Dear Customer,
We detected an unusual sign-in to your account from Moscow, Russia. For your protection your account has been temporarily suspended.
You must verify your identity within 12 hours or your account will be permanently closed.
clues: The sender domain isn't the bank's real domain (northvalebank.com); it just contains the brand name
Generic greeting: 'Dear Customer'
Fear plus a deadline: suspended, 12 hours, permanently closed
The link uses plain http and goes to the look-alike domain

subject: Your parcel is on hold – £1.45 redelivery fee
body: We attempted to deliver your parcel today but no one was available.
To schedule a redelivery please pay the outstanding fee of £1.45. Unpaid parcels are returned to sender after 48 hours.
clues: Tiny fee scams are designed to collect your full card details
A .info domain that isn't the courier's real site
No tracking number, item or sender mentioned
Deadline pressure: 48 hours

subject: Your Brightdesk invoice for October
body: Hi Jordan,
Your monthly invoice for the Team plan (5 seats) is ready. The amount of $60.00 will be charged to the card ending 4417 on 1 November.
You can view or download invoices any time from Settings → Billing in your account.
clues: Sender and link both use the company's real domain
It uses your name and specific details you can check (plan, seats, last 4 digits)
No urgency or threats
It tells you how to get there yourself without the link. Doing that is always the safest option.

subject: Action required: mailbox storage full
body: Your mailbox has exceeded its storage limit (99.8%). You will no longer be able to send or receive emails.
Re-validate your email username and password below to receive an additional 50GB of free storage.
clues: Internal IT would email from your company's own domain, not a '-helpdesk' look-alike
Asking you to 're-validate credentials' is a classic password harvest
Free storage reward plus a threat of losing email
Check with IT directly through your usual ticket system

subject: Bin collection changes over the holidays
body: Hello,
Collections during the week of 22 December will move one day later than usual. Garden waste collections will pause until 6 January.
Full dates for your street are on our website.
clues: Official government domain for sender and link
Purely informational: no login, payment or personal data requested
Nothing urgent or threatening

subject: Quick favour
body: Are you at your desk? I'm in back-to-back meetings and need you to handle something discreetly.
I need 6 x $200 gift cards for a client appreciation surprise. Buy them and send me the codes by email. I'll reimburse you later today. Please keep this between us.
clues: The CEO writing from a personal Gmail address
Gift cards are untraceable, which is why scammers love them
Secrecy ('keep this between us') stops you checking with anyone
Busy-boss pretext so you won't call. Call them anyway.

subject: New this week: 3 shows we think you'll like
body: Hi Sam,
Based on what you've been watching, here are this week's picks.
Manage email preferences or unsubscribe at the bottom of this message.
clues: Real company domain for sender and link
Marketing content with no request for login or payment
Standard unsubscribe option

subject: Priya Shah shared "Q3 Salary Review.xlsx" with you
body: Priya Shah (priya.shah@halcyon-labs.co) has shared a file with you.
Q3 Salary Review.xlsx
Sign in with your work email and password to view.
clues: The sender looks real, but the link goes to a free hosting domain (web.app), not cloudvault.com
The colleague's domain is subtly wrong (halcyon-labs.co vs halcyonlabs.com)
A juicy file name (salary review) to spark curiosity
Asks you to type your work password into the page

subject: Your statement is ready
body: Your October statement is now available.
For your security, we never include links to sign in. Open the Northvale app or type northvalebank.com into your browser to view it.
clues: Real bank domain
Deliberately contains no login link and tells you to go there yourself
No urgency, no request for information

subject: RE: Update to your direct deposit details
body: Hi,
Following up on your request to change your bank account for payroll. Please confirm by replying with your new account and sort code before Friday's cut-off so your salary isn't delayed.
clues: You never asked to change your bank details. The 'RE:' fakes an existing conversation.
Even from a real-looking address, the account could be compromised or spoofed
Asks you to send banking details by email
Deadline plus fear of a delayed salary. Confirm in person or through the HR portal.
